patients.summary: Healthy young personal trainer and amateur bodybuilder who joined from pediatrics at 18. In 2024 a urology workup for trouble conceiving found undisclosed performance-enhancer (androgen) use, which he stopped; in early 2026, after his last practice visit, urology found a left varicocele and is watching it.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is 18 and aging out of his pediatrician's office, looking for an adult doctor close to Amherst. Still on his parents' insurance, card info taken. Booked new pt physical 6/8 at 9:20. Release of records form emailed so he can send it to the pediatric office.

documents.title: New Patient Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
18M establishing adult primary care, coming over from his pediatric office. Just graduated high school and has been working at a gym in town as a personal trainer, picking up clients and doing his certification coursework. Feels well. No complaints today.

PMH: none. No hospitalizations.
PSH: none.
Meds: none. Occasional protein shakes.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Family: mother has hypothyroidism. Father had a left-sided varicocele. No other family history he knows of.
Social: lives with his parents in Amherst. Never smoked, no vaping. Does not drink. Lifts most days, trains clients evenings. Has a girlfriend.
Immunizations: two Pfizer doses at a pharmacy in April (card seen). Childhood records requested.

ROS negative for chest pain, shortness of breath, palpitations, abdominal pain, urinary symptoms, rash, mood problems.

Exam: vitals as recorded. Fit, well-developed young man in no distress. HEENT normal, TMs clear. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin without rash. Normal gait and strength.

PHQ-2 0.

A/P: healthy 18 y/o, well visit.
- Vaccines: confirm HPV and meningococcal from pediatric records when they come in. Flu in the fall.
- Talked about sleep, sunscreen, seat belts, safe sex. He declined STI testing today.
- Physical yearly.

documents.title: Records from prior pediatric practice
documents.author: pediatrics
documents.body:
Pediatric practice transfer summary, patient seen there from infancy through age 18.

Problems: none active. Routine well-child care throughout, growth and development normal.
Medications: none.
Allergies: NKDA.
Immunizations: all routine childhood series complete. Tdap at 11. HPV series complete (2 doses, ages 11 and 12). MenACWY at 11 and booster at 16. Influenza most seasons.
Last well visit at 17: normal exam, normal vision and hearing screens.

Reviewed by PCP, immunizations abstracted to chart.

documents.title: Influenza vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In for seasonal flu vaccine. Feeling well, no fever, no prior reactions. Given left deltoid IM, lot and expiration in MAR. VIS given. Tolerated well, left after brief observation.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
19M for yearly physical. Now certified and training clients full time, plus his own lifting 5-6 days a week. Started doing some physique shows with a friend from the gym. Eats a lot of protein, tracks macros. Up about 4 kg over the year, he says mostly muscle. No concerns.

No meds. NKDA. Non-smoker, no alcohol. Same girlfriend, monogamous.

ROS: negative.

Exam: well-appearing, very muscular build. Vitals reviewed. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Skin clear. No edema.

PHQ-2 0.

A/P: well visit.
- One-time HIV and hepatitis C screening today, he agreed.
- Flu shot this fall, COVID booster then too.
- Fine to keep up the training; reminded him to be careful with any supplements beyond protein and to tell me about anything new.
- Back in a year.

documents.title: Your screening results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Malcolm, both screening tests from Tuesday came back negative (HIV and hepatitis C). Nothing to do. These are one-time screens unless something changes.

documents.title: Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Came in after his last client of the day. Flu vaccine R deltoid, bivalent COVID booster L deltoid. Screening questions negative. Observed 15 min, no issues.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
20M, physical. Early slot before his 9 o'clock client. Competed in two amateur bodybuilding shows this year and is prepping for another in the spring. Weight up again, about 4 kg since last summer; he puts it down to a long building phase and heavy training. Diet very structured, high protein. Denies any new prescriptions. Sleeping ok. Still with his girlfriend.

NKDA. No meds. Never smoker, no alcohol.

ROS: no chest pain, palpitations, headaches, shortness of breath. Mood fine.

Exam: vitals reviewed, BP normal. Heavily muscled. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen benign. No edema.

PHQ-2 0.

A/P: well young adult.
- Lipid panel today since he has never had one and eats a lot of animal protein.
- Flu shot in October.
- RTC 1 year.

documents.title: Cholesterol results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Cholesterol panel looks good, all values in the normal range. No changes needed. See you next summer.

documents.title: Influenza vaccine
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Flu vaccine given L deltoid. No contraindications. Declined the updated COVID shot today, may get it at a pharmacy later. Left in good condition.

documents.title: Cancelled appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt called to cancel tomorrow morning, has a competition this weekend and is cutting weight, doesn't want to come in. Said he'd call back to rebook later in the summer.

documents.title: Question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, my girlfriend and I have been trying for a baby since around January and nothing yet. Her periods are regular, she tracks them on an app. Is there something I should get checked on my end? Not sure if this is something you do or if I need someone else.

documents.title: RE: Question
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good question, and yes, it makes sense to look at both partners. Let's get you in to talk it through and I can send you to the right place. The front desk will reach out with a time next week. Your partner should check in with her own doctor as well.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
21M here about fertility. He and his girlfriend have been trying to conceive since about January, so roughly 9 months, having regular intercourse. Her cycles are regular per her tracking app; she is seeing her own gynecologist. He has never had an STI that he knows of, no genital surgery or injury, no testicular pain. No erection problems. Missed his July physical for a show.

Family: father had a left varicocele; he recently learned an uncle on his dad's side had trouble having children for a male reason. Mother hypothyroid.
Meds: none prescribed. Protein powder and "the usual gym supplements", couldn't name them all.
NKDA. Never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: vitals reviewed, BP normal. Weight 91 kg, very muscular. Heart and lungs normal. GU exam deferred to urology at his preference.

A/P:
1. Trying to conceive, 9 months. Under a year, but given the family history he'd like to be seen now and I think that's reasonable. Referred to urology for evaluation and semen analysis. Asked him to bring a list of every supplement and product he takes to that visit.
2. Tdap due (last at 11), given today.
3. Physical to be rescheduled; flu shot next month.

documents.title: Influenza vaccine
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Seasonal flu vaccine R deltoid. No fever, no egg or vaccine reactions. Pt confirmed urology appt next month. Tolerated without issue.

documents.title: Urology consultation
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Outside urology group, consultation. Date of service 11/18/2024.
Referred by primary care for difficulty conceiving.

Thank you for sending this 22-year-old man, who has been trying to conceive with his female partner for 10 months with regular intercourse. Her cycles are regular per her app. He reports no prior sexually transmitted infection and no genitourinary operations.

He competes in amateur bodybuilding and keeps a strict high-protein diet with intense resistance training. He has put on a great deal of muscle over the last two years, which he credits to discipline and supplements. With more direct questions he acknowledged using performance-enhancing products he buys online; he would not or could not say exactly which ones. He has noticed more acne on the face and back and some mood swings. Libido is normal and erections are not a problem. Body hair has increased; he shaves his chest and arms. Voice deep. No breast enlargement, no testicular pain, has not noticed any change in testicular size.

PMH: none. PSH: none.
Medications: no prescriptions.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: father with left-sided varicocele; paternal uncle with male factor infertility; mother with hypothyroidism.
Social: never smoker, no alcohol. Works as a personal trainer.

Exam: well-appearing, markedly muscular young man. Penis normal. Both testes descended and small for his age, without masses. No varicocele on either side. Epididymides and cords otherwise unremarkable.

Impression:
1. Exogenous androgen use, likely anabolic agents from the history and exam.
2. Male infertility, most likely from suppression of his own testosterone and sperm production by those products.

Plan: we talked at length about how these products shut down the body's own hormone signals to the testes, and that recovery usually takes months after stopping. He agreed to stop all of them now. Hormone tests drawn today and a semen analysis to be done next week. We will send results. Follow-up here in about a year, sooner if anything changes.

Allergies: NKDA. Medications: none.

documents.title: Urology results letter
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Outside urology group, results letter to patient and primary care.

Blood work drawn 11/18/2024: LH and FSH both below the reference range. Total testosterone 1,140 ng/dL.
Semen analysis 11/26/2024: sperm concentration 4 million/mL.

This pattern fits suppression from outside androgens: high testosterone from the products, with his own pituitary signals turned down and low sperm production as a result. Plan unchanged: stay off all performance-enhancing products, and we will recheck labs and a semen analysis at his visit in about a year.

Allergies: NKDA.

Received and scanned. Reviewed by PCP; problem list already updated from the consult.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
22M following up after his urology consult in November. Read their letter and results with him: performance-enhancer use, with low LH/FSH, total testosterone 1,140 and sperm concentration 4 million/mL on the semen analysis.

He says he stopped everything the week after that visit, late November, and has not used anything since. Pretty open about it today, embarrassed he hadn't mentioned it before. Some loss of size and strength, which bothers him for competing, but he's decided a family matters more. Mood has been steady, no low mood or irritability he's worried about. Skin a little better. Still trying with his girlfriend.

Meds: none. NKDA.

Exam: vitals reviewed, weight 89 kg (down 2 from September). Heart RRR, lungs clear. Skin: some acne on upper back. No breast tissue.

PHQ-9 2.

A/P:
1. Exogenous androgen use, stopped late Nov 2024. Supportive; he knows recovery can be slow. Baseline CBC, CMP and lipids today since he was on these products for a while.
2. Male infertility, followed by urology, recheck there in about a year.
3. Physical in the fall.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your blood count, kidney and liver tests all came back normal. Cholesterol is fine too: LDL a touch over 100, which is nothing to act on at your age. Good news overall.

documents.title: RE: Lab results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thanks, that's a relief.

documents.title: Urology follow up
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Should I be going back to urology sooner than they said? Still nothing on the baby front. Still clean since November.

documents.title: RE: Urology follow up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Their plan was to recheck around a year after you stopped, because it often takes that long for sperm production to come back. Winter is the right time. If you want to move it up, you can call their office directly, no new referral needed. Hang in there.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
22M, annual physical. Off all performance products about 11 months now, nothing since late November last year. Training natural; took this season off from competing. Feels fine. He and his girlfriend are still trying, no pregnancy yet. Urology follow-up with repeat semen analysis is due this winter and he plans to book it. No pain, no urinary symptoms.

Problems: exogenous androgen use (stopped), male infertility (urology).
Meds: none. NKDA. Never smoker, no alcohol.

ROS: negative.

Exam: vitals reviewed, weight 88 kg. Well-appearing, muscular. HEENT normal. Neck no thyroid enlargement. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin clear today. No edema.

PHQ-9 1.

A/P: healthy 22 y/o.
- Labs normal in January, nothing needed today.
- Flu vaccine given. Declined COVID.
- Book the urology follow-up this winter.
- Physical next fall.

documents.title: Urology follow-up
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Outside urology group, follow-up visit. Date of service 01/30/2026.

23-year-old man back for infertility follow-up, now about 2 years of unprotected intercourse with his partner without a pregnancy. Since his last visit he has developed left groin discomfort that has gradually increased; he describes it as a dull ache. No injury, no urinary symptoms, no recent infections. He reports no alcohol, tobacco or drug use and has stayed off all performance-enhancing products since November 2024.

PMH: exogenous androgen use, stopped. PSH: none. Medications: none. Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: father with left varicocele; paternal uncle with male factor infertility; mother with hypothyroidism.

Exam: healthy appearing. Secondary sexual characteristics normal. Testes symmetric in size. No redness, swelling or visible mass of the genitalia. Examined standing and while bearing down, there are dilated veins of the left pampiniform plexus.

Labs: testosterone and FSH in the normal range.

Impression:
1. Suspected left varicocele, new since the last exam, with dull left groin ache.
2. Male infertility. Hormones have recovered off androgens.

Plan: scrotal ultrasound to confirm. For the infertility we will take an observation and monitoring approach for now. Will write again with the ultrasound.

reports.text:
Outside urology group imaging. Indication: suspected left varicocele, left groin ache.
Technique: grayscale and color flow imaging of both hemiscrota, at rest and with the patient bearing down.
Findings: The testes are symmetric in size with normal homogeneous echotexture and normal blood flow. No intratesticular mass. Epididymides normal. No hydrocele. On the left, the pampiniform veins are dilated, measuring up to 3.6 mm, with reflux on bearing down. On the right, no dilated veins and no reflux.
reports.conclusion: Left varicocele. Normal testes. No mass or hydrocele.

documents.title: Urology note: ultrasound review
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Outside urology group. Date of service 02/12/2026.

Ultrasound today confirms a left varicocele (veins up to 3.6 mm with reflux on bearing down); testes normal and symmetric.

Assessment: left varicocele; male infertility.
Plan: observation and monitoring. Supportive underwear or a scrotal support for the ache. Repeat semen analysis and visit here in about 6 months. He knows to call sooner if the pain gets worse.

Medications: none. Allergies: NKDA.

Filed to chart as received.

documents.title: Urology update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: FYI urology found a varicocele on the left side, same thing my dad had. They're just watching it for now and I go back in the summer. Hormones are back to normal at least.

documents.title: RE: Urology update
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for letting me know, I have their letters and the ultrasound. Glad your hormone levels have come back. Watching it is a reasonable plan, and they'll go over options at the summer visit. Reach out any time.
